overall_summary: Analysis of deduplicated observations weighted by recent 7-day performance reveals that space/astronomy 'What If' scenarios and bizarre planetary facts dominate the top-performing content. Videos focusing on hypothetical planetary immersion (e.g., liquid diamond, burning ice) and extreme cosmic phenomena (e.g., Venus day/year ratio, TrES-2b dark planet) achieve the highest views-per-day and engagement (likes-per-view). Conversely, older psychological and minor biological factoids show stagnation and lower velocity.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' generated over 1,000 and 972 views respectively within a compressed post-publication timeframe with strong like ratios.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on 'What If you fell into...' formats focusing on extreme, visually striking exotic exoplanets or cosmic anomalies.

winning_patterns.evidence: Titles featuring counter-intuitive planetary rules like 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal' pulled near 1,000+ views rapidly.
winning_patterns.action: Highlight physics-defying celestial mechanics and stark visual contrasts in space.

weak_patterns.evidence: Topics like 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' and general memory facts stagnated under 100 views with minimal engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize mundane psychological life-hacks in favor of high-concept cosmic and physical mysteries.

weak_patterns.evidence: Basic biology facts (e.g., octopus hearts) underperform compared to extreme space scenarios unless paired with an elite comparative hook.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid simple listicle-style animal facts unless integrated into a grander comparative scale narrative.
